I've sent the survey of the six pixel-art files back to the main agent. `rect` is the main helper in all five art files, `disc` comes second, and only textures.ts and estate.ts use `box`.

| File | Draw functions | Biggest function | Most-used pix.ts helpers |
|---|---|---|---|
| textures.ts | 16 | `drawShip` (~62 lines) | rect, INK, disc |
| estate.ts | 7 | `drawHollow` (~98) | rect, WOOD_INK, disc |
| decorart.ts | 1 (plus 34 inline `draw:` entries) | `rover` entry (~64) | rect, INK, disc |
| officeart.ts | 8 | `drawOfficeTower` (~87) | rect, INK, disc |
| cutart.ts | 17 | `drawBust` (~237) | rect, hash, INK |
| pix.ts | 0 | none (shared helpers only) | none |

Function sizes are approximate: I measured from one top-level declaration to the next.

- **textures.ts:** its largest function overall is `buildTextures` (~200 lines), but that isn't a draw function.
- **estate.ts:** it has 17 small building-block helpers of its own (walls, windows, domes and so on), and its draw functions are assembled from those.
- **cutart.ts:** most of its draw functions take a Phaser scene and return a texture key. It uses `hash` (random noise) far more than the other files, 42 times.
- **Outline colour name:** estate.ts, decorart.ts and officeart.ts import the outline colour as `O`. In estate.ts `O` means the wood-brown outline (`WOOD_INK`); in the other two it means the standard dark outline (`INK`).
